title: Retry storms and metastable collapse
summary: A retry budget is the difference between a bad minute and an outage that never clears once the original cause is gone.

steps.title: Before the spike: all three policies look identical
body: Three runs, identical except for retry policy: none, a 3-attempt policy capped at a 10% retry budget, and 3 attempts with no budget at all. All start with a queue depth around 2.
The load spike is a jump to three times normal for forty seconds, then a return to normal. Nothing has happened yet.
steps.look_for: Queue depth flat and low across the fleet before the spike arrives.

steps.title: During the spike, this run has no retry budget
body: This run is the unbudgeted policy: 3 retry attempts, no cap on what fraction of traffic may be retries. Each timeout during the spike adds load precisely when the fleet is least able to absorb it.
A request that times out after twenty seconds has already consumed twenty seconds of device time producing tokens nobody will read — retries here are far more expensive than in a stateless service.
steps.look_for: Queue depth climbing well past its pre-spike level of 2 while the retry count in the corner rises fast.

steps.title: The retry count: 35,806 against 3,841
body: This run reaches 35,806 retries by the end. The budgeted policy (3 attempts, 10% cap) reaches only 3,841 — a ninefold difference — because the cap stops retries from compounding the very overload that caused them.
Goodput here ends at 7,344 tok/s, 46.3% attainment. The no-retry policy ends at 20,161 tok/s, 84.5%. The budgeted policy ends at 17,373 tok/s, 81.1%.
steps.look_for: The goodput line for this run sitting far below the other two, with retries still climbing.

steps.title: Offered load is back to normal. This run never comes back.
body: The spike ended at 40 seconds in; by now load has been back to normal for well over a minute. This run's queue is still about 3x its pre-spike depth (2 to 6) at the end of the run.
That is a metastable collapse: the system is in a state it sustains on its own, and the original cause is gone. The budgeted and no-retry runs both recover, queue 2 to 2.
steps.look_for: Open the A/B view with A = no budget, B = 10% budget. Queue depth in A stays elevated; in B it returns to 2.

steps.title: Invisible in the balancer's own metric
body: Load imbalance is 0.22 to 0.25 in all three runs, essentially identical, even though one of them has collapsed and two have not.

A 10% retry budget recovers 86% of the no-retry goodput (17,373 vs 20,161) and turns the collapse into a recovery. Not smarter routing, not more capacity — just a cap on how much of the offered load may be retries.
steps.look_for: The imbalance panel reading nearly the same number across all three, while goodput tells three different stories.
